metadata.note: The Winchester and Potomac Rail Road (chartered 8 Apr 1831, opened 1836): Harpers Ferry - Charles Town - Winchester, about 32 mi, joined to the B&O at Harpers Ferry from Jan 1837. The company ran its own trains until the Civil War; the Union army seized it on 12 Mar 1862. From Jan 1866 the Baltimore and Ohio ran the trains (temporary arrangement, then a lease from 1 Jul 1867; the B&O bought the W&P in 1902), and from 20 Jun 1870 extended them over the Winchester and Strasburg Railroad to Strasburg as its Valley Branch. Passenger service ended 13 Aug 1949; the line is still the CSX Shenandoah Subdivision. Four features: the W&P era in its own new colour, and three B&O features in the existing 'Baltimore and Ohio Railroad' string and colour (read programmatically from baltimore_and_ohio_mainstem.geojson), split at Stephenson's and Winchester because each piece has a different first confirmed year. The W&P feature shares the B&O features' Harpers Ferry - Winchester geometry (Rule 4 split by operator).
metadata.source: research/branches/winchester_and_potomac_railroad.txt (2026-10-27): Virginia Free Press and Spirit of Jefferson items catalogued on the Jefferson County WV History wiki; W&P annual report 1865 (csa-railroads.com); Wikipedia 'Winchester and Potomac Railroad', 'Shenandoah Subdivision' (citing the Baltimore Sun 1870 and 1949, The News 1949, ICC valuation 1934) and 'Harpers Ferry station'; Official Guide Feb 1952 Table 62 and index.
metadata.freight_only_check: Harpers Ferry - Strasburg after 13 Aug 1949 is freight only (Official Guide Feb 1952 Table 62 'Freight Service only' and index daggers on Halltown, Summit Point, Kernstown, Charles Town B&O) and still CSX freight today - not drawn. Civil War military operation 1862-1864 (Union supply and troop trains) and 1861 Confederate movements are not public passenger service and are not drawn. The adjacent PRR Hagerstown - Winchester and Winchester and Western lines are other roads and are not in this layer.
metadata.horsecar_check: None found, none trimmed: a steam locomotive made the first run on 9 Mar 1836, before public operations began on 14 Mar 1836 (Virginia Free Press 10, 17, 24 Mar 1836).
metadata.ownership_split: Rule 4 split at Jan 1866, when the B&O began running the trains (a temporary operating arrangement counts; the 1 Jul 1867 lease formalised it). The W&P feature (1836-1858) and the B&O features (1866/1867/1870-1949) share geometry and do not overlap in years. Not splits: the 1902 B&O purchase of the W&P (corporate; the B&O already ran the trains), the Winchester and Strasburg roadbed company (B&O-operated from opening), and the 1987 CSX merger (after passenger service).
branches_deliberately_omitted: Report block [2] - government trains Harpers Ferry - Stephenson's, 1865 [ANCHOR]: omitted. Public timetables with a ticket agent (Virginia Free Press 31 Aug, 14 Sep, 2 Nov 1865) show public passenger service, but which government body ran them (U.S. Military Railroads, another federal custodian, or the Virginia Board of Public Works) is unresolved, so no company/colour can be assigned. The report says omitting it is the safe choice; it must never be folded into the W&P or B&O feature.
Report block [6] - Strasburg - Harrisonburg (old Manassas Gap extension, later Southern): drawable NONE; operator and years unsourced.
Report block [7] - Valley Railroad / B&O Harrisonburg - Staunton - Lexington: drawable NONE; candidate for its own research run. The 1942-43 abandonment/sale dates are not passenger end dates.
Strasburg Junction - Strasburg station (1.2 mi over the Manassas Gap / Southern track): not drawn; already drawn by the Manassas Gap layer, and the B&O passenger terminal there is unresolved.
not_yet_sourced: W&P pre-war END is OPEN: drawn to 1858, the last confirmed year (W&P notice dated 12 Aug 1858). Service almost certainly continued, by an unproven amount, up to the military seizure of 12 Mar 1862. Wanted: an 1859-1861 W&P schedule or passenger notice (Alexandria Gazette, Richmond Dispatch, Staunton Spectator via Chronicling America were not searched - loc.gov was rate-limiting). Two 1861 items (a 17 Jun 1861 militia transport certificate; Thomas R. Sharp's 1861 diary) suggest the line worked in mid-1861 but are not public-passenger evidence.
1865 operator name (block [2], omitted): 'Government' in the local paper; USMRR vs Virginia Board of Public Works not settled.

1866-1867 operator conflict: two Jan 1866 items say the B&O ran the trains; a June 1866 item calls a brakeman a W&P employee and the May 1867 timetable is signed by the W&P president. Drawn as B&O from 1866. The defensible fallback, if that is rejected, is B&O from 1867 with 1866 omitted - not 1866 under the W&P.
When trains reached Winchester again after the war: between Aug 1865 (Stephenson's only) and May 1867. Stephenson's - Winchester is drawn from 1867, the first confirmed year.
Which Strasburg terminal B&O passenger trains used (Strasburg Junction, 50.3 mi, or Strasburg, 51.5 mi).

Valley Branch frequency in every year except 1867 (two round trips a day) and 'a single daily round trip' near the 1949 end; no pre-1949 Official Guide table was read. The 1870 Winchester - Strasburg opening rests on one newspaper cite via Wikipedia.
W&P frequency 1836-1857 and all running times; avg_speed_kmh is an estimate on every feature.
Original 1836 strap-rail alignment and the 1836 Virginius Island depot approach at Harpers Ferry: not traced; the W&P feature is drawn on the later B&O/CSX alignment.

properties.line: Winchester and Potomac: Harpers Ferry – Winchester
properties.speed_source: estimate for a strap-rail (16.5 lb/yd flat bar on wooden stringers) steam road of the 1830s-50s; no running time was read for any year

properties.geometry_quality: Traced from OpenStreetMap end to end, no straight-line legs: 31.8 mi drawn against 31.4 mi documented (Official Guide Feb 1952 Table 62) / 31.5 mi (Wikipedia W&P station table) / 32 mi (Wikipedia W&P). All but about 0.1 mi on ways tagged old_railway_operator=B&O, 'Shenandoah Subdivision'. LATER ALIGNMENT THAN ITS ERA (Rule 2): this 1836-1858 feature is drawn on the B&O / CSX Shenandoah Subdivision as it exists today, not on the original 1836 strap-rail alignment, which was repeatedly destroyed and rebuilt in the Civil War (1862-1864) and relaid by the B&O after 1866; where the original line departed from today's track is not established. The Harpers Ferry end is drawn at today's junction with the B&O main line at the west end of the Potomac bridge (the post-January 1837 connection); the 1836 Virginius Island depot terminus is NOT drawn. The Winchester end is the vertex nearest the Nominatim centroid of Winchester (0.3 km off the line); the W&P's own Winchester depot site was not pinned. Simplified Douglas-Peucker 8 m, then trim_reversals.

segments.note: Winchester and Potomac's own trains, Harpers Ferry - Halltown - Charles Town - Cameron's Depot - Summit Point - Stephenson's Depot - Winchester. Steam from the first trip: the locomotive Tennessee ran Virginius Island depot - Winchester on 9 Mar 1836 and public operations began 14 Mar 1836 (Virginia Free Press 10, 17, 24, 31 Mar 1836; Wikipedia citing Dilts p. 191); no horse traction to trim (Rule 5). Connected to the B&O by its first Potomac bridge in Jan 1837. Continuity: W&P schedules and fare advertisements in Charlestown papers 1837, 1838, 1843, 1853, 1855, 1856, an 1857 account of riding the road, and the Aug 1858 passenger-train notice. END IS OPEN: 1858 is the LAST CONFIRMED year (W&P notice dated 12 Aug 1858, Virginia Free Press), NOT a known end. Service almost certainly ran later, by an unproven amount, up to the Union military seizure of 12 Mar 1862 (W&P annual report 1865); no 1859-1861 public passenger item was found. Do not extend without evidence, and do not close to 1861 on inference. 1862-1864 was military-only operation and is not drawn. headway_min 1440 = one round trip a day (Winchester dep. 9 am, Harpers Ferry dep. 1:30 pm), SOURCED for 1858 only; frequency 1836-1857 is NOT SOURCED.
sources: Segment-level: Virginia Free Press 10, 17, 24, 31 Mar 1836 (opening, steam from the first trip); W&P notice in the Virginia Free Press dated 12 Aug 1858 (last confirmed year and the 1858 frequency) - Jefferson History AccessIDs 11100, 11110, 11121, 11124, 17809; W&P annual report 30 Dec 1865 (passengers carried before the war; military seizure 12 Mar 1862)

segments.note: B&O-operated trains over the Winchester and Potomac, Harpers Ferry - Halltown - Charles Town - Cameron's (Aldridge) - Summit Point - Wadesville - Stephenson's Depot. Start 1866: the U.S. Government handed the road bed back to the W&P company and the B&O took 'temporary possession' (Spirit of Jefferson 16 Jan 1866) and ran the trains 'for the present' from about 22 Jan 1866 (Spirit of Jefferson 23 Jan 1866); formal 20-year lease from 1 Jul 1867 (Spirit of Jefferson 17 Dec 1867; ICC 1934 p. 365). The Rule 4 split is at Jan 1866, when the operator changed. SOURCE CONFLICT recorded, not resolved: a June 1866 item calls a brakeman a W&P employee and the May 1867 timetable is signed by the W&P president; the report weights the two explicit Jan 1866 statements that the B&O ran the trains. Drawn only to Stephenson's from 1866 because the 1865 end of track was there and no 1866 source says how far the B&O's trains ran; the Stephenson's - Winchester piece is a separate feature from 1867. End 13 Aug 1949, when passenger service over the branch ended. headway_min 720 = two round trips a day, SOURCED for 1867 only (timetable of 14 May 1867, Spirit of Jefferson 31 Dec 1867). Frequency in every other year is NOT SOURCED, apart from Wikipedia 'Harpers Ferry station' (citing Lee 2003) saying service had dwindled to a single daily round trip before the end. Freight continued after 13 Aug 1949 and the line is still the CSX Shenandoah Subdivision - not drawn (Rule 1).
sources: Segment-level: Spirit of Jefferson 16 and 23 Jan 1866 (B&O takes over, Jan 1866; AccessIDs 6617, 21779); Spirit of Jefferson 17 Dec 1867 (lease from 1 Jul 1867; AccessID 23732) and 31 Dec 1867 (timetable of 14 May 1867, two trains each way; AccessID 23993); 13 Aug 1949 end: Baltimore Sun 'The End of an Era', 18 Sep 1949 p. 61, and The News (Frederick) 19 Aug 1949 p. 11, both as cited by Wikipedia 'Shenandoah Subdivision'; corroborated (after the fact) by the Feb 1952 Official Guide, B&O Table 62 'Harper's Ferry and Strasburg. Freight Service only.' and its index daggers

segments.note: B&O trains Stephenson's Depot - Winchester. Start 1867 is the FIRST CONFIRMED year, not a known start: in Aug 1865 the government trains ran only to Stephenson's and the road 'may ... be continued to Winchester' (Virginia Free Press 31 Aug 1865); the timetable dated 14 May 1867 (printed in the Spirit of Jefferson to 31 Dec 1867) runs two trains each way through to Winchester. Trains may have reached Winchester again in 1866, but no source shows it; if one does, merge this feature into Harpers Ferry - Stephenson's with start 1866. End 13 Aug 1949. headway_min 720 = two round trips a day, SOURCED for 1867 only (timetable of 14 May 1867, Spirit of Jefferson 31 Dec 1867). Frequency in every other year is NOT SOURCED, apart from Wikipedia 'Harpers Ferry station' (citing Lee 2003) saying service had dwindled to a single daily round trip before the end. Freight continued after 13 Aug 1949 and the line is still the CSX Shenandoah Subdivision - not drawn (Rule 1).

NOT DRAWN: the last 1.2 mi from Strasburg Junction east into Strasburg station over the Manassas Gap / Southern track, which the Manassas Gap layer already draws, and which terminal B&O passenger trains actually used is unresolved. segments.note: B&O trains Winchester - Kernstown - Bartonville - Stephens City - Middletown - Strasburg Junction - Strasburg over the Winchester and Strasburg Railroad (incorporated 23 Apr 1867), opened 20 Jun 1870 and leased to the B&O 'from the outset' (ICC 1934 p. 362), so B&O-operated from the first day - same operator as the Harpers Ferry - Winchester features, no Rule 4 split. Opening date from a single newspaper cite (Baltimore Sun 22 Jun 1870 p. 2, via Wikipedia); no 1870 passenger timetable was seen, but the 1871 and 1873 combined B&O/W&P schedule ads are consistent. End 13 Aug 1949: the end of passenger service applies to 'the branch', Harpers Ferry - Strasburg. headway_min 720 is NOT SOURCED for this section in any year - carried over from the 1867 Harpers Ferry - Winchester timetable as an estimate; near the end service was a single daily round trip (Wikipedia 'Harpers Ferry station', citing Lee 2003). Connected at Strasburg with the old Manassas Gap line (Southern), whose passenger years are drawn in its own layer. Freight continued after 13 Aug 1949 and the line is still the CSX Shenandoah Subdivision - not drawn (Rule 1).
